title: catch-up 2: per-provider entitlement ranges (the participation-window MUST)
description:
docs/design/mimi-catchup.md §8, and the part the note says implementers will get wrong.

The hub must record, per room and per provider, the sequence ranges during which that provider had a participant. A catch-up answer is bounded by them: nothing from before its first participant joined, nothing from after its last left. Otherwise catch-up becomes a retroactive read of a room the provider was removed from, which is a worse hole than the one being closed.

This is the main NEW STATE the design needs. The hub already tracks the participant list and the Commits that change it; what it does not keep is the mapping from those changes to §4's sequences. Design that mapping before writing the serving code.

Tests, each showing a wrong provider is refused, as AGENTS.md requires of an authorization boundary: a provider that joined at sequence 500 is refused 1 to 499; one that left at 900 is refused 901 onward; one that was never a participant is refused everything; one that left and rejoined gets both of its ranges and not the gap between them.
